solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Circling Lima, glower in the direction of American flyer

indicators.note: to circle something is to go right round it, so one piece surrounds another

parts.note: a light bulb is a thing that glows, a 'glower'
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet
as in throwing something at a target

explanation.surface: Someone scowls at an American bird while circling the Peruvian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glower' looks like a verb meaning scowl, but it is a noun: something that glows. Lima is the capital of Peru on the surface and the phonetic letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: The bullbat is a North American nighthawk, a bird, so it is literally a flyer found in America.

clue.text: One flexes lighter company earnings per share

parts.note: Bic is a company famous for disposable lighters and pens
the standard financial abbreviation

explanation.surface: A business report: a lighter manufacturer flexes its muscles with its earnings per share figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One flexes' reads like a company showing strength, but it defines a muscle: the biceps is what you flex to show strength.
explanation.definitionFit: The biceps is the upper-arm muscle people tense to show off, so it is the thing someone flexes.

clue.text: Producer of light satire flips a bit?

indicators.note: in binary a bit flips from 0 to 1, so one O-shaped zero becomes an I-shaped one

parts.note: a lampoon is a piece of satire mocking a person

explanation.surface: A question about whether satire has gone slightly over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: The computing joke in 'flips a bit': a bit is a binary digit, and flipping it turns 0 into 1, so one O of LAMPOON becomes I.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampion is an old-fashioned oil lamp, often of coloured glass, which produces illumination.

clue.text: Automatic exclusion of European country dismissing core constituents

indicators.note: dismissing sends away, and the core is the centre, so the middle letters are removed

parts.note: a ban excludes someone
the adjective for Austria; its central TR is dropped

explanation.surface: A European country is automatically shut out after losing key members.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European country' must be read as the adjective AUSTRIAN, whose two central letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Banausian is a rare word for mechanical or merely utilitarian, so a routine, machine-like action counts.

clue.text: Persistently sore during lifting exercises, suffers from rising sloth and babbling

indicators.note: something happening during another event sits within it in time, so one piece goes inside another
in a down clue, lifting raises letters so they read from bottom to top

parts.note: physical training
aching continually
as in 'has a cold'

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means reading the letters upward

parts.note: the ai is a three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: Someone with aching muscles after weightlifting suffers from laziness and talks nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sloth' looks like the sin of laziness, but it is the animal, the three-toed ai beloved of setters. Both 'lifting' and 'rising' turn letters upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Tachyphasia is abnormally rapid, often unintelligible speech, a medical term covering voluble babbling.

clue.text: Set price of one last letter after divvy

parts.note: a divvy is British slang for a fool
Roman numeral
the British name for Z

explanation.surface: After a share-out, the price of one final letter is fixed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divvy' suggests a share-out (dividend), but here it is British slang for an idiot. 'After' puts the fool first.
explanation.definitionFit: To assize was formerly to fix the price or standard of goods such as bread by official decree.

clue.text: Laurel's partner undressed, which was a slightly harrowing thing

definitions.text: which was a slightly harrowing thing

indicators.note: stripped of its outer layer, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: Oliver Hardy was the partner of Stan Laurel in the comedy double act

explanation.surface: A comic image of a famous comedian's sidekick stripped bare, which proved mildly distressing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Undressed' strips HARDY of its outer letters. 'Harrowing' looks emotional but is agricultural: an ard only scratched the soil, so it harrowed slightly; 'was' because it is an ancient tool.
explanation.definitionFit: An ard is a primitive light plough that scratched a shallow furrow rather than turning the soil over.

clue.text: Sentimental drivel — abridged edition's opening Miltonic floodgate

indicators.note: an abridged text is shortened, so the final letter is cut

parts.note: slush is mawkish sentimentality

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses an abridged Milton edition as sentimental drivel opening the floodgates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Miltonic' signals an archaic spelling used by Milton for the word now spelt sluice.
explanation.definitionFit: A sluice is a gate controlling the flow of water, and Milton spelt the word this way in his poetry.

clue.text: Zulu against turning to Greek islander

parts.note: Zulu is Z in the NATO phonetic alphabet
anti means opposed to

indicators.note: turning round makes the letters face the other way

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A Zulu, once opposed, comes round to a native of a Greek island.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the little word 'to' is turned; Z and ANTI stay as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zantiot is a native or inhabitant of Zante, the Ionian island also called Zakynthos.

clue.text: Recall years experimental composer headed university department

indicators.note: to recall is to call back, so the letters go back the other way

parts.note: standard abbreviation
John Cage, the American experimental composer
led as in was at the head of

explanation.surface: Someone remembers the years when an avant-garde composer ran a university department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recall years' looks like reminiscing, but 'Recall' turns the whole string round. John Cage is famous for the silent piece 4'33".
explanation.definitionFit: At Oxford and other universities a delegacy is a committee or body administering a particular area, effectively a department.

clue.text: It's like hurling a crew into hidden eastern deserts

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it
to desert is to abandon, so this letter leaves the word

parts.note: cached means stored away out of sight
standard abbreviation for east
taken as written
to man a vessel is to crew it

explanation.surface: Like flinging a ship's crew into remote eastern deserts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserts' looks like a noun for arid lands but is the verb, abandoning. Hurling is an Irish stick-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: Camanachd is the Gaelic name for shinty, a Scottish game closely related to Irish hurling.

clue.text: Brand of comedy struck from logbook of large vessels

indicators.note: something struck from a record is crossed out and removed

parts.note: a ship's journal is its log
Jo Brand is a British stand-up comedian

explanation.surface: A comic label removed from the record book of big ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brand of comedy' reads like a style of humour, but it is Jo Brand, a well-known British comedian. Dropping her first name from JOURNAL leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Urnal is an adjective formed from urn, meaning relating to urns, which are large vases or containers.

clue.text: After cycling, perhaps prepare for massage in private at Picardy

indicators.note: cycling rotates a sequence, moving letters from one end round to the other

parts.note: one might oil up before a massage

explanation.surface: After a bike ride, a soldier gets ready for a rub-down in his quarters in northern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Private' looks like an adjective about the massage, but it is a soldier's rank. Move the last letter of OIL UP to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Poilu was the nickname for a French infantryman in the First World War, much of which was fought in Picardy.

clue.text: Starchy vegetable base for pavlova with 25 per cent less rhubarb we hear?

definitions.note: the chatter heard, a noun sense of the -ing form

indicators.note: losing a quarter of an eight-letter word cuts two letters from it

parts.note: the yam is a starchy tuber
a pavlova is built on a meringue base

explanation.surface: A cookery note: a vegetable-based pavlova with less rhubarb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rhubarb' is not the fruit for the pavlova but the word actors mutter to suggest background chatter. Two of MERINGUE's eight letters go.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is noisy meaningless talk, and yammering is persistent loud chatter, so what we hear is the same din.

clue.text: Reading up on verse (I somehow almost could) at my own risk

indicators.note: reading upward in a down entry takes the letters in the opposite order

parts.note: re means on the subject of
a poem is a piece of verse

indicators.note: done somehow means done in some unspecified way, so the letters can be put in any order
almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, losing its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone studying poetry, unsure of their ability, admits they read it at their own peril.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reading up' sounds like studying, but in a down entry it tells you to read the letters upwards. The answer is a Latin phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Meo periculo is Latin for 'at my peril', a phrase used to accept personal responsibility for the danger.

clue.text: Warning: hot piece of firewood is clamped by worker possibly in charge, counteracting heat

indicators.note: a clamp grips from both sides, so outer letters close around the inner ones

parts.note: the worker is a caste of ant
standard abbreviation, i/c
a tip-off is a warning
H for hot, as on a tap
a log is cut for the fire
taken as written

explanation.surface: A safety warning: a hot log held by a supervising worker, to fight the heat.
explanation.walkthrough: The worker and the in-charge abbreviation join as the word ANTIC, which opens after its second letter to hold everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Antiphlogistic means reducing inflammation, and inflammation is a heating of body tissue, so it acts against heat.

clue.text: Using the language of English limits endlessly checking place of colon

indicators.note: limits are boundaries on either side, so these letters enclose what follows

parts.note: 'in E', E being English

indicators.note: without its end, a word loses its final letter

parts.note: testing means checking

explanation.surface: A grammar note about English and where the colon goes when checking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colon' looks like the punctuation mark, which suits the grammar surface, but it is the bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is the main part of the large intestine, so that organ is where the colon is found.

clue.text: Good hindquarters go quickly for the old Scottish pig

parts.note: standard abbreviation
the rump is the hind part of an animal
an old word meaning hasten

explanation.surface: An old Scots pig with fine hindquarters runs off quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Hie is an archaic verb for hurry, common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumphie is a Scots dialect name for a pig, from its grunting, now rather dated.

clue.text: Material wrapping small bouquet, one of remembrance

indicators.note: wrapping something means folding round it, so outer letters surround the rest

parts.note: material in the sense of physical, actual
mini means small
a wine's bouquet is its scent
Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Fabric wrapped round a small posy, kept as a keepsake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Material' looks like a noun for cloth, but it is the adjective meaning actual. 'Bouquet' is the smell of a wine, not flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Reminiscential means relating to reminiscence, the act of recalling past events, which is remembering.

clue.text: Crew member got up, available for hire before noon

indicators.note: getting up means rising, and in a down entry rising reads the letters bottom to top

parts.note: a 'to let' sign advertises property for rent
ante meridiem

explanation.surface: A sailor rose early and offered himself for hire in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Got up' reads like waking, but it turns the whole string upward in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British slang, from French, for a sailor, so a member of a ship's crew.

clue.text: American musical female leads first person who's indigenous to India

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: one who is

parts.note: standard abbreviation
divas are leading female singers
the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: An American female musical star introduces the first Indian native.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leads' looks like a verb, but 'female leads' is a noun phrase for star singers.
explanation.definitionFit: Adivasi is the collective name for India's tribal peoples, regarded as its original inhabitants.

clue.text: Giant with conjoined bodies admitted to surgery once

indicators.note: a patient admitted to hospital is taken inside, so the letters lie within the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the two words

explanation.surface: Conjoined twins who were once admitted to surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The hospital surface of conjoined patients and surgery hides a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Geryon was the monstrous giant of Greek myth with three bodies joined at the waist, killed by Heracles.

clue.text: Flash opera provided returning boats for Venetians

parts.note: a mo is a moment, as is a flash
Puccini's opera

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: if means on condition that

explanation.surface: A showy opera supplied boats coming back for the people of Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flash' looks like an adjective meaning showy, but it is a noun: an instant.
explanation.definitionFit: Motoscafi are the Italian motorboats, plural of motoscafo, used as water taxis in Venice.

clue.text: Shrew is cross in two ways

parts.note: sore means annoyed, cross
an X is a cross, the second sense

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered woman is angry twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shrew' suggests a scolding woman, but it is the animal. 'Cross in two ways' gives the angry sense and then the mark X.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorex is the scientific genus name of the common shrews, small insect-eating mammals.

clue.text: Wrap up one's bung

parts.note: 'wrap up' is slang for be quiet, and sh means hush
one's read as 'one has', I've

explanation.surface: Someone wraps up their cork or stopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wrap up' is British slang for shut up, and 'one's' expands to 'one has', which is I'VE.
explanation.definitionFit: A shive is a flat cork or wooden stopper for a cask or wide-mouthed bottle, the same thing as a bung.

clue.text: Merriment's more than half related to organ pipe openings?

indicators.note: keeping more than half of a word means the rest is dropped

parts.note: hilarity is merriment

explanation.surface: Fun about the openings of organ pipes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ pipe' suggests the musical instrument, but the organ is a bodily one, like a lung or kidney, with tubes entering it. Five of HILARITY's eight letters stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilar relates to a hilum, the notch in an organ where vessels, ducts and nerves enter and leave.

clue.text: Article used for cooking squashes growing from a stem

indicators.note: to squash is to squeeze in, so one piece is pressed inside another

parts.note: culinary means to do with cooking
the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A kitchen utensil for cooking squashes and other plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Squashes' looks like the vegetable, fitting the kitchen surface, but it is the verb: the cooking word squeezes in the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Cauline and caulinary are botanical terms for leaves or parts arising from the plant's main stem.

clue.text: Notes from Scarlatti provide MacMillan's drive

parts.note: read the composer's name and keep only the letters that are musical note names, which come in order as the answer

explanation.surface: Music by an Italian composer supposedly giving a Scottish composer his motivation.
explanation.walkthrough: Of the letters S-C-A-R-L-A-T-T-I only C, A and A name musical notes; the rest are discarded. James MacMillan is a Scottish composer, signalling a Scots word: caa means to drive, as cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect, caa means to drive or propel, as in driving livestock along a road.

clue.text: Team in Europe leaves for Cup, maybe being easily made to run

parts.note: the European Union

indicators.note: one thing in another sits inside it

parts.note: tea leaves are what goes into a cup of tea
a cricket or football team has eleven players

explanation.surface: A European team departs for a Cup competition, ready to run easily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves for Cup' sounds like a team setting off for a trophy match; it is tea leaves for a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: Eutexia is the property of being easily melted, and melted metal runs, so to run means to melt here.

clue.text: Award celebrity a point behind the crown

parts.note: Order of the British Empire, an honour
a social lion is a celebrity

explanation.surface: A celebrity receives an honour, standing just behind the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The crown' suggests the monarch handing out honours; here it is the top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: The obelion is a point on the skull between the parietal foramina, towards the back of the crown of the head.
